newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE'S 1996 EU FUND ABSORPTION IS SATISFACTORY.
newsitem.headline: GREECE'S 1996 EU FUND ABSORPTION IS SATISFACTORY.

text.p: Greece's European Union (EU) funds' absorption rate was satisfactory in 1996, the head of the EU Cohesion Fund told a news conference on Wednesday.
"In 1996, the absorption rate has been higher than in 1995. Greece is in the top list of countries aided by the Cohesion Fund," said Jean Francois Verstrynge, the head of the Cohesion Fund.
Four monitoring committees are responsible for supervising progress on transportation, the environment, the Spata airport and the Evinos dam projects.
The focus of the Cohesion Fund is on transportation and environmental infrastructure projects, he said.
Overall, progress in the transportation sector in Greece has been made. The Cohesion Fund has also financed a study of a better coordination of means of transportation.
Significant environmental projects include wastewater plants in Psyttalia, Crete, Patras and Korinth. The Psyttalia project is the biggest in Europe, he said.
Some pilot projects for islands have also been established. Studies are conducted on the treatment of waste for the islands of Mykonos and Aegina or the desalination of water in Santorini, he said.
"Our aim is to develop new technologies in Greece. We have no attachment to any particular foreign company as has been said," he added. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
